title: Momentum-resolved quantum noise spectroscopy using ensembles of diamond quantum sensors
authors: Zeeshawn Kazi, Kai-Hung Cheng, Jared Rovny, Nathalie P. de Leon
abstract: Spatiotemporal fluctuations across multiple scales govern and characterize the emergent properties, phase boundaries, and low-energy excitations of strongly correlated matter. However, capturing these dynamics has remained a major experimental challenge, as conventional probes typically offer either high spatial or temporal resolution, but not both simultaneously. Here, we leverage high-fidelity wide-field imaging of dense diamond nitrogen vacancy center ensembles to measure the momentum and frequency power spectral density of magnetic fluctuations. To access spatial wavevectors below the diffraction limit, we tune the sensing volume continuously through optical depletion. This approach enables study of equilibrium and driven fluctuations across three orders of magnitude in spatial scale and tunable frequency bands, providing a direct means to map low-energy, long-wavelength fluctuations in correlated systems.
summary: This work presents a novel technique using wide-field imaging of diamond NV ensembles to measure the momentum-resolved magnetic noise power spectral density. By measuring two-point correlations across large areas, the authors overcome the resolution limits of conventional probes. This allows for the direct mapping of low-energy, long-wavelength magnetic fluctuations critical for understanding strongly correlated materials.
main_problem: Characterizing spatiotemporal fluctuations in strongly correlated matter is challenging because conventional probes lack simultaneous high spatial and temporal resolution.
main_result: The technique successfully measures the momentum-resolved magnetic noise power spectral density, $S(\mathbf{q}, \omega_0)$, by leveraging wide-field correlation measurements.
method: The authors use wide-field imaging of diamond NV ensembles to measure two-point magnetic correlations, which are then Fourier transformed to obtain the momentum-resolved spectral density.
model_or_system: The physical system is a solid-state platform using dense ensembles of diamond nitrogen vacancy (NV) centers. The measurement probes magnetic fluctuations, relating the measured noise variance to the dynamical structure factor.
key_observables: Momentum-resolved magnetic noise power spectral density $S(\mathbf{q}, \omega_0)$, and real-space magnetic field correlation maps.
important_parameters: Spatial wavevectors ($\mathbf{q}$) spanning three orders of magnitude, and tunable frequency bands ($\omega_0$).
main_assumptions: The method assumes the noise structure factor can be reconstructed by Fourier transforming the measured two-point correlation function, and the wide-field measurement assumes translational symmetry.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the process of mapping magnetic field correlations, computing the Fourier transform to reveal finite momentum features, and detailing the wide-field spin-to-charge conversion (SCC) readout.
paper_structure: The paper develops the theoretical framework for measuring $S(\mathbf{q}, \omega_0)$ using correlation functions, details the wide-field and sub-diffraction measurement schemes, and presents results showing the ability to resolve anisotropic and periodic fluctuations.
why_interesting: The use of quantum sensors (NV centers) to probe collective, low-energy, long-wavelength fluctuations in correlated matter bridges quantum optics, condensed matter physics, and advanced sensing techniques.
